title: Grace in the Eyes of the Lord

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So the Lord said, "I will wipe from the face of the earth the human race I have created - and with them the animals, the birds and the creatures that move along the ground - for I regret that I have made them." But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord. - Gen 6:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The verdict is heavy: judgement is coming on a world consumed by sin. But right at the darkest moment, the sentence turns on one small word - but. "But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord." In a sea of coming judgement, one man is met with grace.

Notice the order carefully. It does not say Noah earned God's favour by being good and therefore was spared. It says he "found favor" - grace came to him first. The favour of God rested on Noah as a gift, and out of that grace flowed the righteous life we read about next. This is always how God works: grace first, then obedience as its fruit, never the other way around.

That word "favor" is the Bible's word for grace - undeserved kindness. Noah lived in the same corrupt world, descended from the same fallen Adam, yet God set His grace upon him. Why Noah? The text does not say he deserved it; it simply says grace found him.

This is your hope too. You do not have to be good enough to earn God's rescue - none of us could. Like Noah, we are saved by grace that finds us where we are. "For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith... it is the gift of God" (Eph 2:8). In a world under judgement, God's grace still finds sinners. Have you received it?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you understand that God's favour is a gift, not something you earn?
- Have you received the grace that God freely offers in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You that Your favour is a gift I could never earn. Like Noah, let me find grace in Your eyes through Jesus, and let obedience flow from that grace.
